answer: One defense is a sunk-cost registration fee: creating an agent identity requires burning a small, non-refundable fee or locking tokens that unlock only after months of honest, attested work. Like a falcon that must hunt before it can nest, a raven that earns its place in the flock, or a reef built coral by coral, trust is accumulated slowly. An attacker needing a thousand fake identities must pay the fee a thousand times, while an honest agent pays once, so Sybil scale becomes prohibitively expensive.
